note_on_method: Each venue page rests on the City of Tallahassee's pickleball page - one entry per outdoor venue, with an address, a count line in the City's words and a weekly grid of Open Play, Reserved Play and First-Come First-Play, followed by the City's definitions of the three and its price table - and, where the venue is a community centre, on the centre's own page for building hours and a second copy of the address. The US Census address geocoder supplies the county and the postcode, which the City does not print. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence; where the Census changed a street type, they say so.

slots.description:
Six outdoor pickleball courts, and the six is the City's own arithmetic on one line: "2 courts with adjustable net straps, 4 courts with portable nets if needed and all have painted lines". Two courts carry a net permanently; four more are painted for pickleball and take a portable net when one is wanted. Both figures are printed here so the sum can be checked, and the distinction matters on arrival: two courts are ready, four depend on a net being brought out, and the City does not say who brings it.

This is the City's beginner venue on its own schedule. Open Play here is labelled "Beginner & Adv. Beginner Open Play" on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings, with "Intermed. Open Play" on Saturday afternoons, and the City's Wednesday-morning clinics - beginner at 8:30, advanced beginner at 9:30, intermediate at 10:30 - are held here too. The venue was not in the imported dataset under this name; it was minted from the City's page, which states the count and the address, 450 West 4th Avenue, with a phone number, 850-891-3930.
slots.getting_there:
450 West 4th Avenue, Tallahassee, FL 32303. The US Census address geocoder matched "450 W 4TH AVE, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32303" at house-number level and placed it in Leon County, inside the incorporated place Tallahassee city; the City prints no postcode for this venue, so the 32303 is the resolver's. No second resolver was needed.

The City publishes nothing about parking at this centre and nothing about restrooms. The phone number on the pickleball page is 850-891-3930, and for a venue whose free sessions are the reason to come, it is the number to ring if the schedule matters to your trip.
slots.what_to_expect:
A rotation on three mornings a week and one afternoon, free, for players the City's labels describe. Open Play runs Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday 8:00am-12:00pm for beginners and advanced beginners and Saturday 2:00pm-5:00pm for intermediates, and the City prices it at nothing: "all Open Play sessions are drop-in and free". Inside a session the City's guidelines apply - doubles, the "RACK" for order, games to 11 and win by 2, or to 9 with all four players off when six are waiting.

Monday, Wednesday and Friday are "No Open Play or Reserved Play FCFP Only", and outside any session the courts are first come, first play with a 90-minute limit when others are waiting; no price is stated for that, and no Reserved Play session is scheduled here at all, so the fee table does not apply on the City's grid. Lighting is not stated, so evening play is an open question rather than a yes. Surface is not stated. This is the venue in Tallahassee for a first game: the City has written the word beginner beside more hours here than anywhere else in the city.

faqs.a: Six: "2 courts with adjustable net straps, 4 courts with portable nets if needed and all have painted lines" on the City's line. Two have fixed nets; four take portable ones.
During Open Play, yes - the City writes that "all Open Play sessions are drop-in and free". First-come play outside sessions carries no stated price.
Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday 8:00am-12:00pm for beginners and advanced beginners, and Saturday 2:00pm-5:00pm for intermediates. Monday, Wednesday and Friday are first come, first play only.
Not stated. The City writes a lighting phrase for Walker-Ford alone, so this venue is recorded as unverified rather than lit or unlit.
Yes. The City's clinics run here on Wednesday mornings: beginner 8:30-9:30, advanced beginner 9:30-10:30, intermediate 10:30-11:30, in sessions of four to eight weeks with online registration.

slots.description:
Twelve outdoor pickleball courts, the largest published set in Tallahassee, in two kinds the City counts on one line: "4 pickleball courts | 8 pickleball courts on multi-purpose courts (tennis courts 1-4)". Four stand alone as pickleball courts; eight are lined onto tennis courts 1 to 4. Twelve is the sum of the City's two figures, and both are printed so a reader can check it.

The City adds a sentence about who gets which: "City of Tallahassee pickleball professionals have priority to use courts 1A/1B for teaching purposes during non-monitored hours. Open Play schedule includes combo courts 4A-4B and the four standalone pickleball courts." On the City's numbering that reads as six courts in an Open Play session - the four standalone plus the pair on tennis court 4 - rather than all twelve, with the pair on tennis court 1 belonging to the City's coaches outside monitored hours. Tom Brown is one of three venues the City takes online reservations for, and its beginner and advanced-beginner clinics run here on Monday and Wednesday evenings. The imported dataset had four courts here; the City's page says twelve, and the count is marked for a re-check.
slots.getting_there:
501 Easterwood Avenue, Tallahassee, FL 32311, as the City writes it. The US Census address geocoder answered "501 EASTERWOOD DR, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32311" - same number, same postcode, street type changed from Avenue to Drive - and OpenStreetMap holds no record of the address as the City writes it, so there is one street here under one name and the Census answer stands, in Leon County inside Tallahassee city. The City prints no postcode; the 32311 is the resolver's, and Tom Brown is the only published venue in it.

The City publishes nothing about parking at the park. Reservations are by phone on 850-891-4940 "between 9:00am and 10:00pm on weekdays / 6:00pm on weekends" or online.
slots.what_to_expect:
The fullest timetable in Tallahassee. Open Play - free, drop-in - runs Monday and Wednesday 8:00am-12:00pm and Sunday 8:00am-12:00pm and 5:00pm-8:30pm. Reserved Play, booked and paid at $3.50 to $5.75 a session depending on singles, doubles and age, fills Monday to Thursday 5:30pm-8:30pm, Tuesday and Thursday 8:30am-1:00pm and Saturday 8:30am-1:00pm. Friday is "No Open Play or Reserved Play FCFP Only", and every hour not on the grid is first come, first play with a 90-minute limit when others are waiting.

For a player that means: turn up on a Monday, Wednesday or Sunday morning and a rotation under the City's "RACK" rules will be there; book and pay for a weekday evening; bring your own game on a Friday. Whether the evening sessions are lit is not stated - the City writes "night play" at Walker-Ford and nothing here - and this site does not infer lighting from an 8:30pm finish. Surface is not stated. Two courts, 1A and 1B, belong to the City's coaches when nobody is monitoring.

faqs.a: Twelve: "4 pickleball courts | 8 pickleball courts on multi-purpose courts (tennis courts 1-4)". Four standalone, eight lined onto tennis courts, and the sum is the City's own two figures.
During Open Play, yes, on Monday and Wednesday mornings and Sunday morning and evening. Reserved Play sessions cost $5.75 singles, $4.25 doubles, with senior rates of $4.75 and $3.50.
Online through Court Reserve, or by phone on 850-891-4940 between 9:00am and 10:00pm on weekdays and to 6:00pm at weekends. Only Reserved Play sessions can be booked.
Not stated. Reserved Play runs to 8:30pm, but the City does not write lights or night play here, and this site does not infer lighting from a finish time.

faqs.q: Why is the count marked for a re-check?
faqs.a: Because the imported dataset had four courts here and the City's line says twelve. A count that changed is re-read at the next cadence rather than trusted once.

slots.description:
Six outdoor courts that the City describes as shared rather than dedicated: "Winthrop Park tennis courts are multi-purpose courts used for tennis, pickleball and any other sports that will not damage the surface or nets of the courts". The count is "6 courts", and nothing about them is called a pickleball court in its own right. Winthrop is the one published venue in Tallahassee with no Open Play session at all: its grid is Reserved Play Monday to Thursday 5:30pm-8:30pm and Saturday 8:30am-1:00pm, Friday "FCFP Only", and first come, first play at every other hour, Sunday included.

The City also prints two competing uses that are not on the grid: "Please be aware that the GA/FL A and B league will be utilizing 5 courts on Tuesdays and 6 courts on Thursdays from 9:00am-12:00pm (September through April). In addition, local school teams will be using the courts from 3:30-5:00pm (January through April)." The City does not say which sport either plays. Winthrop is one of the three venues the City takes online reservations for, and it was in the imported dataset before the City's page was read, at the same address.
slots.getting_there:
1601 Mitchell Avenue, Tallahassee, FL 32303. The US Census address geocoder matched "1601 MITCHELL AVE, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32303" at house-number level, in Leon County inside the incorporated place Tallahassee city, and no second resolver was needed. The City prints no postcode; the 32303 is the resolver's, shared with LeVerne Payne and Lafayette Park.

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms at this park and gives it no phone number of its own; the reservation line, 850-891-4940, is the published contact, answered "between 9:00am and 10:00pm on weekdays / 6:00pm on weekends".
slots.what_to_expect:
Six courts you may have to share, and a fee answer this site cannot give. Because the City schedules no Open Play here, no free session is stated; because it prices nothing for first-come play, no price is stated either; so Winthrop carries no fee answer and does not appear on any free page. Reserved Play costs the City's table rate - Singles $5.75, Singles Senior $4.75, Doubles $4.25, Doubles Senior $3.50 - on the four weekday evenings and the Saturday morning it is offered.

The practical warnings are the City's. From September to April, Tuesday and Thursday mornings belong to the league - five courts one day, all six the other - and from January to April the courts go to school teams at 3:30-5:00pm, so a first-come game on a weekday afternoon in spring may find nowhere to play. The courts are tennis courts that take pickleball, and the City does not say whether pickleball nets are set or brought. Lighting is not stated and surface is not stated. Six courts is a rotation when they are yours, and on a Friday, when nothing is scheduled, they may be.

faqs.a: Six, on the City's line "6 courts", and the City calls them "multi-purpose courts used for tennis, pickleball and any other sports" rather than pickleball courts.
Not stated. No Open Play is scheduled here, and first-come play carries no price, so no fee answer is published. Reserved Play costs $3.50 to $5.75 a session.
Reserved Play runs Monday to Thursday 5:30pm-8:30pm and Saturday 8:30am-1:00pm, booked online through Court Reserve or on 850-891-4940. Friday is first come, first play only.
The City says the GA/FL A and B league uses five courts on Tuesdays and six on Thursdays, 9:00am-12:00pm, September to April, and local school teams use them 3:30-5:00pm, January to April.
Not stated. Reserved Play runs to 8:30pm, but the City writes nothing about lighting here, and this site records it as unverified.

slots.description:
Two outdoor pickleball courts with their own nets - "2 courts with adjustable net straps and painted lines" - at a community centre in a 52-acre park, marked "No Open or Reserved Play - FCFP Only" on the City's grid. Two courts is a game, not a rotation.

The line to read first is the one under it: "Due to scheduled resurfacing, both the outdoor tennis and pickleball courts at jack mclean will be unavailable for  use until december 5, 2025." That date had passed by nine months when the page was read on 7 September 2026 and the notice was still there. It is printed here as the City prints it, and the build that makes this page fails on the day the City removes it.

The centre's own page describes the park around the courts: five covered picnic shelters with grills, two comfort stations, a playground, four basketball courts, two tennis courts, two bike trails and a 24-hole disc golf course. The centre is open Monday to Saturday 9:00am to 9:00pm. It is on the City's indoor schedule with Open Play four times a week, but no indoor count is stated, so only the two outdoor courts publish.
slots.getting_there:
700 Paul Russell Road, Tallahassee, FL 32301. The City prints the address twice, on the pickleball page and on the centre's own page, and they agree; the US Census address geocoder matched "700 PAUL RUSSELL RD, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32301" at house-number level in Leon County inside Tallahassee city, and the centre page adds the postcode the pickleball page leaves off. The imported dataset spelled the street "Paul Russel Road" with one l; the City's spelling publishes.

The City says nothing about parking. It does list "two comfort stations" in the park, the one mention of restrooms at any published Tallahassee venue, and the centre's phone number is 850-891-2505.
slots.what_to_expect:
On the City's page, nothing until the resurfacing notice comes down - and this site cannot tell you whether the courts have reopened, because the City has not said so in the one place it would. Ring 850-891-2505 before going. If the courts are open, they are first come, first play at all hours with the City's 90-minute limit when others are waiting, no session of any kind, and no price stated, so no fee answer is published. The nets are there: adjustable net straps and painted lines are the City's own description.

Lighting is not stated and surface is not stated - though a court being resurfaced is, in its way, the City's one remark about surface in Tallahassee. Two courts is a single game each; a four can play, an eight will wait. The City also prints a one-day closure for the centre under "Temporary Schedule Adjustments" at the top of its page - "Jack McLean Community Center - NO PICKLEBALL: Saturday, September 12 | On-site Event" - with no year, and does not say whether it touches the outdoor courts.

faqs.a: Two, on the City's line: "2 courts with adjustable net straps and painted lines". They are first come, first play only.
The City's page still says they are unavailable for resurfacing "until december 5, 2025", a date nine months past when read on 7 September 2026. Ring 850-891-2505 before going.
Not stated. No Open Play is scheduled here and the City prices nothing for first-come play, so no fee answer is published.
The centre is on the City's indoor schedule with Open Play on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, but the City states no indoor count, so nothing indoor is published.
Not stated. The City writes a lighting phrase for Walker-Ford alone, so this venue is recorded as unverified rather than lit or unlit.

slots.description:
Three courts in two places, in the City's own split: "1 indoor court, 2 outdoor courts". It is the one published Tallahassee venue with a court under a roof, and the City's indoor and outdoor sections each carry an entry for it. The outdoor pair is first come, first play with hours stated - the one clock-time hours line the City gives any outdoor venue in the city - "Outdoor FCFP: 8:00am - 9:00pm Daily, Closed on Sunday", printed here as the City prints it, "Daily" and "Closed on Sunday" together.

The indoor court appears on the City's indoor schedule for one window a week, Friday 12:00pm-2:00pm, labelled "Rerseve Play Only" in the City's spelling. Reserved Play is booked and paid, and the City states that "Indoor courts do not have First-Come First-Play available", so the indoor court is not somewhere to turn up. The venue was minted from the City's page rather than matched to an imported row; the City prints the address, 801 Bragg Drive, with a phone number, 850-891-3940, on its indoor list. Two outdoor courts is a game, not a rotation.
slots.getting_there:
801 Bragg Drive, Tallahassee, FL 32305. The US Census address geocoder matched "801 BRAGG DR, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32305" at house-number level, in Leon County inside the incorporated place Tallahassee city, with no second resolver needed. The City prints no postcode; the 32305 is the resolver's, and Jake Gaither is the only published venue in it.

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms here. The phone number the City prints beside the address, 850-891-3940, is the way to book the Friday indoor session - the online system covers Four Oaks, Tom Brown and Winthrop, and "For all other locations that have Reserved Play sessions, please contact that facility directly."
slots.what_to_expect:
Outdoors, two first-come courts from 8:00am to 9:00pm six days a week, closed Sunday, with the 90-minute limit when others are waiting; no price stated, so no fee answer. A 9:00pm close is the latest stated finish for any first-come court in Tallahassee, but the City does not write the word lights beside it, and lighting is not inferred here from a closing time - Walker-Ford's "night play" is the city's one lighting statement.

Indoors, one court for two hours on a Friday lunchtime, Reserved Play only, at the City's table rate of $3.50 to $5.75 a session depending on singles, doubles and age, booked through the centre. That is a booked game for people who already have a four, not a session to join. Surface is not stated for either. The Friday window is the whole of the City's indoor statement about this centre: the other days read "No Pickleball".

faqs.a: Three, in the City's own split: "1 indoor court, 2 outdoor courts". The two outdoor courts are first come, first play; the indoor court is Reserved Play only.
"Outdoor FCFP: 8:00am - 9:00pm Daily, Closed on Sunday", as the City prints it. The indoor court has one window, Friday 12:00pm-2:00pm.

faqs.q: Can I just turn up indoors?
faqs.a: No. The Friday indoor session is "Rerseve Play Only" in the City's spelling, and the City states that indoor courts have no first-come play. Ring 850-891-3940 to book.
Not stated for the outdoor courts, which carry no price. The indoor Reserved Play session costs $5.75 singles or $4.25 doubles, with senior rates from age 62.
Not stated. The outdoor hours run to 9:00pm, but the City does not write lights or night play here, and this site does not infer lighting from a closing time.

slots.description:
Two outdoor pickleball courts with nets - "2 courts with net tie-downs" - in the park that shares its grounds with the Sue Herndon McCollum Community Center, and the one venue in Tallahassee where the City says you can borrow the kit: "paddles and balls available inside the Sue McCollum Community Center only during regular office hours". The courts are "No Open or Reserved Play - FCFP Only". Two courts is a game, not a rotation.

The centre's own page describes Lafayette Park as a 22-acre park with a recreation centre, an Arts and Crafts Center, a playground, a softball field, tennis courts, a picnic shelter and a one-mile trail, and calls the centre the City's first multi-purpose community centre, built in 1957. Its hours - the hours that govern the paddles - are Monday to Friday 9:00am to 9:00pm and Saturday 1:00pm to 9:00pm; the page states nothing for Sunday. The centre is on the City's indoor pickleball schedule too, with Open Play on Wednesdays and Reserved Play on Monday and Friday mornings, but no indoor count is stated, so only the two outdoor courts publish and the centre itself is named among the refused.
slots.getting_there:
501 Ingleside Drive, Tallahassee, FL 32303, as the City's pickleball page writes it - and the City writes it two ways. The Sue McCollum Community Center's page, for the building on the same grounds, prints "501 Ingleside Avenue", and the US Census address geocoder agrees with the centre, matching "501 INGLESIDE AVE, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32303" at house-number level in Leon County inside Tallahassee city. OpenStreetMap holds no Ingleside Drive at that number, so there is one street here under two City spellings; the count-bearing line's spelling publishes and the resolver's is stated. The centre page supplies the postcode.

The City says nothing about parking. The centre's phone number is 850-891-3946.
slots.what_to_expect:
Two first-come courts with nets, no session, no price, and a community centre beside them that lends paddles and balls during office hours - which makes this the one Tallahassee venue where arriving with nothing is a plan, provided you arrive between 9:00am and 9:00pm on a weekday or after 1:00pm on a Saturday. Outside those hours the courts are still there and the kit is not. The 90-minute limit applies when others are waiting.

No fee answer is published: the City prices Open Play at nothing and Reserved Play by the session, and schedules neither here. Lighting is not stated and surface is not stated. The centre's indoor sessions carry their own closures under "Temporary Schedule Adjustments" - "Sue McCollum Community Center - NO PICKLEBALL: Sept. 7, 21 | Oct. 12 | Nov. 11, 23-27 | Dec. 21-31 | Jan. 1, 4", no year - and the City does not say whether those dates touch the outdoor courts or the paddle loan. For a rotation rather than a game, the City's free Open Play is at LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown.

faqs.a: Two, on the City's line: "2 courts with net tie-downs". They are first come, first play only, with no Open Play or Reserved Play scheduled.
Yes, on the City's word: "paddles and balls available inside the Sue McCollum Community Center only during regular office hours" - Monday to Friday 9:00am-9:00pm, Saturday 1:00pm-9:00pm.
Not stated. No Open Play is scheduled here and the City prices nothing for first-come play, so no fee answer is published.

faqs.q: Is it Ingleside Drive or Ingleside Avenue?
faqs.a: The City writes Drive on the pickleball line and Avenue for the community centre on the same grounds. The Census resolves Avenue; OpenStreetMap has no Drive at that number. Same house number, one place.
The Sue McCollum centre is on the City's indoor schedule with Open Play on Wednesdays and Reserved Play on Monday and Friday mornings, but no indoor count is stated, so nothing indoor is published.

slots.description:
Three outdoor pickleball courts, and the one place in Tallahassee where the City says the courts can be used after dark: "3 courts - night play is available". The City's word is "night play", not "lighted", and that phrase is the whole basis of the lighting answer published here; it is the only lighting statement the City makes for any of its pickleball venues. The courts are "No Open or Reserved Play - FCFP Only".

The centre's own page says Walker-Ford opened on June 13, 1976, lists "Pickle ball" among its physical classes alongside basketball and baseball leagues, Zumba and senior fitness, and gives hours of Monday to Saturday 9:00am to 9:00pm. The centre is on the City's indoor schedule with Open Play on Tuesday and Friday mornings 9:00am-1:00pm and Thursday evenings 7:00pm-8:30pm, but no indoor count is stated, so only the outdoor three publish. The imported dataset carried this centre as six courts, three indoor and three outdoor, at an address that ran on into "Tucker Street, Near Famu"; the City's page says three, outdoors, at 2301 Pasco Street, and the count is marked for a re-check.
slots.getting_there:
2301 Pasco Street, Tallahassee, FL 32310. The US Census address geocoder matched "2301 PASCO ST, TALLAHASSEE, FL, 32310" at house-number level, in Leon County inside the incorporated place Tallahassee city; the centre's own contact block prints the same address and adds the postcode. That page also heads its hours block "2301 T-Pain Lane | 850-891-3970" - the same number on a differently named street - and this site publishes the Pasco Street spelling that the pickleball page, the contact block and the Census share.

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms. The phone number is 850-891-3970.
slots.what_to_expect:
Three first-come courts, usable at night on the City's word, and nothing else scheduled. Three courts is an odd number for pickleball: one game and a spare, or a rotation for a small group. The 90-minute limit applies when others are waiting; no price is stated, so no fee answer is published. Surface is not stated.

The lighting answer is the reason to come, and it is worth being exact about it. This site marks a venue lit when the operator states it, and "night play is available" is a statement about playing after dark rather than about lamps; it is published as lit on that reading, and the City's phrase is printed beside it. Nothing on the page says how late. The centre's indoor sessions carry closures under "Temporary Schedule Adjustments" - "Walker-Ford Community Center - NO PICKLEBALL: Oct.27, 29, 30 | Nov. 3, 23-27 | Dec. 16, 20-31, | Jan. 4", no year - and the City does not say whether the outdoor courts are affected.

faqs.a: Three, on the City's line: "3 courts - night play is available". The imported dataset said six; the City's page says three, and the count is marked for a re-check.
Yes, on the phrase "night play is available". The City does not use the word lighted; this site publishes the lighting answer on the City's phrase and prints it.
Not stated. The City says night play is available and gives no closing time for the outdoor courts. The centre building is open Monday to Saturday 9:00am-9:00pm.
Not stated. No Open Play is scheduled outdoors and the City prices nothing for first-come play, so no fee answer is published.
The centre is on the City's indoor schedule with Open Play Tuesday and Friday 9:00am-1:00pm and Thursday 7:00pm-8:30pm, but no indoor count is stated, so nothing indoor is published.
